It's so ridiculously easy, you'll love it! First you need a glass jar big enough to hold a bunch of eggs - but if you like pickles, that part is simple.

Solids:

  • 12 hardboiled eggs, peeled
  • 2 white onions, cut coarsely
  • 4 carrots, shaved finely
  • Crushed garlic, the more the merrier
  • Small spoonful of turmeric powder
  • Sprig of dill, chopped very finely
  • 2 or 3 cloves
  • 10 whole peppercorns

I like to add extra salt when making my brine solution - for every liter of vinegar I add ~50mL of salt, which is more than double what most recipes call for. I feel like it helps the eggs develop a tough outer layer, which is my favorite part.

Shaving the carrots into thin flakes is to help them release more of that sweet carrot flavor. The onion and carrot slurry that's left over can be scooped out with a fork and spread on top of some spinach for a nice salt-and-vinegar salad topper. If you like crunchy carrot sticks better I can't blame you, but they don't give the eggs as much carrot taste that way.

Lastly, dill is one of those herbs it's absolutely worth growing yourself or buying fresh, over buying those dried-out bottles. It takes almost no work whatsoever and the difference between fresh dill and dried is hard to overstate. Once you start cutting it up, you'll smell what I mean!
